entries.title: Proverbs 28:2
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: But - By a wise and good prince.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: It like - Is like a violent rain or flood, which washes away the very seeds in the earth. He is the worst of all oppressors.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:4
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Contend - Are so far from praising them, that they severely reprove them.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:5
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Judgment - What is just and right. All things - Which are necessary to be known by them.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:10
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Causeth - That by evil counsel, or example, or artifice, draws them into evil.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:12
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Rejoice - Are promoted. Glory - In that common - wealth. Rise - Are advanced to authority. Hidden - Wise and good men, who only are worthy of the name of men, withdraw themselves into obscure places.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:14
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Alway - In all times, companies, and conditions.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:16
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Oppressor - The tyranny of a prince, is a manifest sign of folly. Prolong - By God's favour, the peace and satisfaction of his own mind, and the hearty love of his people.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:17
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Violence - That sheddeth any man's blood. Shall flee - Shall speedily be destroyed. Shall slay - None should desire or endeavour to save him from his deserved punishment.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:18
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: At once - Once for all; so he shall never rise more.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:20
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Faithful - Who deals truly and justly in all his transactions.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:21
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: For - When a man hath once accustomed himself to take bribes, a very small advantage will make him sell justice.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:22
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Evil eye - Is uncharitable to persons in want, and envious to those who get any thing besides him. Poverty - And consequently that he shall need the pity and help of others.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:24
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: The same - Is a thief and robber.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:26
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Wisely - Distrusting his own judgment, and seeking the advice of others, and especially of God.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:28–29:3
entries.author: John Wesley (1703–1791)
entries.content: Men - Righteous men are afraid to appear publickly.
